brief: A true moment from the history of search and SEO (keyword stuffing, PageRank, link farms, Panda, Penguin, mobile-first, featured snippets) told as a story, then what it teaches about being found by AI today.
How AI assistants and AI Overviews choose what to show: one answer instead of ten links, how they pick sources, why some brands get named and others don't.
One practical GEO or AEO tactic (structured data, llms.txt, quotable answers, FAQs, entity clarity, being cited by trusted sites) explained with a before-and-after.
A technical thing that quietly blocks AI from reading a site (robots.txt rules for AI crawlers, JavaScript-only content, missing canonical tags, no sitemap) and how to check it.
A common SEO or AI-visibility myth and what is actually true, with a clear example.
The difference between being mentioned by an AI (from memory) and being cited (your page used as the source), and why the gap matters.
How local businesses get found in AI answers ('best dentist near me'): consistent business details, reviews, opening hours, and what AI gets wrong about them.
AI agents that visit websites to do tasks for people (find a price, book, fill a form): what makes a site easy or impossible for them to use.
